subject: biology
title: Abiotic and biotic factors
key_idea: **Abiotic** factors are the non-living conditions in an environment, such as light and temperature. **Biotic** factors are the living things that affect a community, such as predators and pathogens. A change in either can change the size of populations.

blocks.text: Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment. This section covers the ones in the specification and how each affects a community.

items.meaning: A non-living factor that can affect a community.
A living factor that can affect a community.

rows: Plants need light for photosynthesis, so less light means less growth and fewer plants.
Affects how fast organisms grow and reproduce, and which species can live in an area.
Organisms need water. Dry conditions reduce the number of plants and animals that can live there.
Plants take in mineral ions from the soil to grow. The pH of the soil affects which plants can grow.
Affects water loss from plants and the spread of seeds and pollen.
Plants need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
Aquatic animals need dissolved oxygen to respire.

blocks.text: To show that an abiotic factor has an effect, compare how many organisms live where the factor is high and where it is low.

items: Abiotic factors are non-living: light, temperature, moisture, soil pH and minerals, wind, carbon dioxide and oxygen.
Say how the factor changes the survival, growth or numbers of the organism.

blocks.text: Biotic factors are the living things in an environment. This section covers the four biotic factors in the specification.

items: **Availability of food:** less food means fewer animals survive and breed.
**New predators arriving:** more prey are eaten, so the prey population falls.
**New pathogens:** disease can kill many organisms in a population.
**One species outcompeting another:** the numbers of the weaker species may no longer be enough to breed.

diagram.alt: Sort each factor into abiotic or biotic.
diagram.prompt: Is each factor abiotic or biotic?

items: Biotic factors are living: food, predators, pathogens and competition.
A new predator, pathogen or competitor can reduce a population.

sections.heading: How a change affects a community

blocks.text: A change in one factor often leads to a chain of effects. Link each step in your answer.
Example: a plant shaded by taller plants

items: Taller plants absorb most of the light, so there is less light for the plants below.
Less light means less photosynthesis, so less glucose for growth.
Where there are fewer trees, more light and more water or minerals reach the soil, so there is less competition and more plant species can grow.
A moth that feeds on oak leaves competes with aphids for the same food.
Aphids have less food, so the number of aphids decreases.
Species further along the food chain, such as ladybirds, may then also decrease.
Link the factor, the effect on the organism, and the change in numbers.
Use competition, food, predation or disease to explain a change in a population.

checks.q: Give two abiotic factors that could affect the size of an earthworm population.
checks.a: Any two from: water / moisture, oxygen / air in the soil, pH of the soil, minerals / ions, temperature, type of soil.

checks.q: Give two biotic factors that could affect the size of an earthworm population.
checks.a: Any two from: food, predators, disease / pathogens.

checks.q: Explain why there are more plant species growing in an area with no trees.
checks.a: More light (and water / minerals) reaches the soil, so there is less competition. More photosynthesis makes more glucose for growth.

worked_example.question:
Earthworms live in soil, feed on dead and decaying plant matter, have soft, moist skin, and exchange gases through their skin.

Give two abiotic factors and two biotic factors that could affect the size of an earthworm population.
answer_points: Abiotic (any two): water / moisture, oxygen / air in the soil, pH of the soil, minerals / ions, temperature, size of soil particles or type of soil.
Biotic (any two): food (or the amount of dead and decaying matter in the soil), predators, disease / pathogens / microorganisms.
worked_example.tip: Two marks for abiotic and two for biotic. Four correct factors in the wrong categories still score 2 marks.

worked_example.question:
A scientist decided to study the variety of living organisms in a garden. The scientist also measured abiotic factors in the garden. The pH of the soil was measured using a pH meter.

Describe how three other abiotic factors could be measured in the garden.
answer_points: Light levels using a light meter (lux meter).
Water in the soil using a water meter or sensor, or from the wet and dry mass of a soil sample.
Rainfall using a measuring cylinder or beaker.
Humidity using a humidity meter or sensor.
Depth of the soil using a ruler.
Wind direction or strength using a wind sock or wind meter.
worked_example.tip: Any three scores one mark each. Name the factor and the instrument.

blocks.text: Pollutants are abiotic factors that can harm organisms.

items: Pollutants include chemicals that make rain or water acidic.
They can kill organisms or reduce how many survive and reproduce.
This can reduce the number of species in a community.

worked_example.question:
A student investigates the effect of acid rain on seed growth. She dips some cotton wool in 20 cm³ of water, puts 20 mustard seeds onto the cotton wool and places it inside a flask. She puts the remaining water into the flask. She repeats this four more times, each time using different solutions of water and dilute sulfuric acid. After 8 days she counts how many of the seeds have germinated.

Volume of water in flask (cm³) | Volume of dilute sulfuric acid in flask (cm³) | Number of seeds that germinated
20 | 0 | 18
16 | 4 | 15
8 | 12 | 13
4 | 16 | 6
0 | 20 | 2

Explain what this experiment shows about the effect of acid rain on seed germination.
answer_points: Acid rain reduces the number of seeds that germinate.
Small volumes of acid have little effect, with a rapid drop in germination between the third and fourth flask.
Some germination is still possible at the highest volume of acid, so the acid would have to be more concentrated to stop germination.
worked_example.tip: Any two points score. Use the data from the table to support the answer.

worked_example.question:
The plants in a woodland are eaten by mice and caterpillars. The mice also eat the caterpillars. The mice are eaten by birds called owls.

A scientist counted the mice and owls on the same summer day each year for five years. The number of mice per km² was 2 × 10³ in year 1, 2 × 10³ in year 2, 3 × 10³ in year 3, 5 × 10³ in year 4 and 1 × 10³ in year 5.

Suggest why there were more mice in year 4 than in the other years.
answer_points: More food available (plants, caterpillars or other food).
Higher birth rate than death rate.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these score one mark each. Fewer owls is not credited.
